ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Hubert H. Humphrey Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: First visit to establish shared care three months after radical cystoprostatectomy with an ileal conduit for bladder cancer. Concerns: Wants his follow-up after bladder removal and his urostomy managed close to home and work; Bothered by appliance leaks and sore skin around the stoma, which interrupt his long working days. [S]

tr.td: Sodium bicarbonate 650 mg oral tablet, one tablet by mouth twice daily, for metabolic acidosis after an ileal conduit
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg oral tablet, one tablet by mouth twice daily for 7 days, for acute pyelonephritis
One tablet twice daily for 7 days

Cystoscopy and transurethral resection of bladder tumors, at the cancer center: recurrent multifocal papillary urothelial carcinoma, low grade, with high-grade carcinoma in situ in random biopsies; muscularis propria present and not invaded (cTa with CIS); small, poorly compliant bladder after earlier radiation
Staging CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis with CT urography: thickened bladder wall; no hydronephrosis, upper-tract filling defect, enlarged lymph nodes, or distant disease

Radical cystoprostatectomy with bilateral pelvic lymph node dissection, partial urethrectomy, and ileal conduit urinary diversion, stoma in the right lower abdomen, at the cancer center. Pathology: multifocal urothelial carcinoma, high grade, with carcinoma in situ, invading the inner half of the muscularis propria (pT2a); 0 of 18 lymph nodes (pN0); ureteric and urethral margins negative; prostate with benign hyperplasia and no urothelial involvement
Renal ultrasound at six months: no hydronephrosis on either side; normal kidney size and cortical thickness; conduit decompressed
Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes

tr.td: First visit to establish shared care three months after radical cystoprostatectomy with an ileal conduit for bladder cancer
Four-week follow-up with urology consultation: surveillance plan, stoma and peristomal skin, and metabolic monitoring
Six-month post-cystectomy follow-up: kidney function, acid-base, upper-tract ultrasound, and review after a kidney infection
Nine-month post-cystectomy follow-up: acid-base on bicarbonate, stoma review, and the surveillance schedule
Same-day sick visit for fever and right flank pain
Urology consultation to share survivorship surveillance after radical cystectomy, review the stoma, and set the metabolic monitoring plan
Cancer surveillance after cystectomy for pT2a N0 disease: CT or MRI of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis every 6 to 12 months for 2 to 3 years, then yearly; no adjuvant therapy

Kidney and metabolic monitoring after an ileal conduit: chemistry with creatinine, chloride, and bicarbonate every 3 to 6 months in the first year, then yearly; upper-tract imaging every 6 months to year 3; vitamin B12 yearly; alkali for bicarbonate below 22 mmol/L
Stoma care with the wound, ostomy, and continence nurse: appliance fitting, peristomal skin care, and parastomal hernia checks

Urine infection plan with a conduit: no routine urine cultures or treatment of bacteriuria without symptoms; for fever, flank pain, or rigors, a culture taken by catheter from the stoma and prompt treatment; about 2 liters of fluid a day
Distress screening at each visit, physical activity, and a written survivorship care plan
Leak-free urostomy appliance with healthy peristomal skin
Appliance refitted with a convex wafer at the consultation; no leaks in the two months after the refit and skin healed
Stable kidney function (creatinine within 0.3 mg/dL of the post-operative baseline) and bicarbonate 22 mmol/L or more
Creatinine 1.10 mg/dL; bicarbonate 24 mmol/L on sodium bicarbonate
Regain stamina after surgery: walk 30 minutes a day and regain weight
Walking 30 minutes most days; weight up 1.1 kg since the first visit
Written survivorship surveillance schedule in place, shared between urology and primary care
Schedule given; CT due at one year after surgery
